reason: Same split-tape problem as Round 2: the Investing.com Fed Rate Monitor (2026-09-15) has the September 16 decision at 90.1% hold / 9.9% cut with no hike priced, while Yahoo Finance's same-day pre-FOMC headline sweep has Wall Street leaning toward pricing in a hike alongside a 10-year yield spike through 5% (highest since 2023/2007-era levels) -- a genuine disagreement between rate-futures-implied and narrative-implied odds that argues against taking a fresh directional rate bet into the print. This book's structure already has natural convexity to that exact disagreement: the long KRE/XLF/IBB legs benefit if the dovish (hold-to-cut) camp is right and financials/biotech catch a relief bid, while the short GDX leg is the correct hedge if the hawkish (hike) camp is right, since higher real yields are historically the single biggest headwind to gold miners -- and that leg is already the book's best performer (+4.25%) into this exact yield spike, which is the market already telling us the hedge is doing its job. KRE sits flat (+0.08%) rather than breaking down, which does not look like a book bracing for a 2023-style regional-bank duration shock despite the 5%+ tenor. Every leg carries a stop (10-15%) that will fire mechanically if the hike scenario hits banks harder than the GDX short can offset. Re-papering the book into a binary 24-hour catalyst would swap a position with a live, partially self-hedging structure and working stops for a fresh cost basis and commission drag with no better information than what is already priced. Reassess once the actual statement and dot plot are in hand.
